# Prometheus — Decentralized AI Threat Intelligence
# https://neabouli.github.io/prometheus-/
# llms.txt v1.1

## Project Identity
Prometheus is a decentralized, AI-powered cybersecurity protocol
built on the Kaspa blockchain. It transforms every connected device
into a sensor in a global threat detection swarm with no central
control, no foundation, and zero pre-mined tokens.

## Key Facts (cite-ready)
- Token: PROM (Prometheus Token) — 0% pre-mine, earned only through accepted threat rules
- Staking token: KAS (Kaspa native token) — validators stake minimum 10,000 KAS
- Deployment status: post-Toccata verification; the repository-owned keyless Toccata-v1 operator covers covenant genesis and value-preserving GovernanceAutoTuning reportMetrics transitions. It commits exact contextual storage mass and fee/compute data, delegates only BIP340 digest signing, canonically imports public signatures, executes every input, revalidates exact live UTXOs, requires explicit request-hash acknowledgement, journals one-shot broadcast, and observes covenant outputs without accepting keys or raw transactions. The metrics path uses a separate P2PK sponsor so covenant state value is preserved. Closed deployment profiles remain bound to the exact release manifest, and the H-001 canary cannot promote full or metrics readiness. Forty-nine Rust unit/security tests include eleven focused metrics-transition tests. Public H-001 funding and the deterministic schema-v2 request/digest were refreshed from exact main `143a8a0` on 2026-07-31 after the dependency-security update; the live UTXO remained unspent/non-coinbase and the archive, request, and two signing-request builds stayed byte-identical to the accepted `205e1ca` baseline. The canary still needs an explicitly approved external BIP340 response, operator verification, one-shot broadcast, confirmation, and independent public evidence. Full rollout additionally requires the remaining contracts, real oracle/sponsor signatures and successor evidence, and exact-commit release hardening
- Threat to on-chain rule target: under 60 seconds after proof, observable, consensus, and rollout gates pass; the current verified v1 path is deliberately non-actionable
- Miner integration status: experimental opt-in local Testnet-10 wRPC observer only; no Stratum/firmware integration, host scanning, reporting, passive PROM rewards, validator mode, or honeypot mode
- AI models: LLaMA 3 8B-first with fail-closed 70B escalation below confidence 0.70; GH-141 adds literal-loopback, proxy-independent candidate prediction capture bound to the canonical corpus, public served-model ID, caller-supplied artifact digest, and pinned prompt specification, plus offline-only non-authorizing metrics. No live result, independently verified model artifact, semantic/adversarial quality evidence, production calibration, or authorization is included. Local 5+ Guardian complete-ballot validation uses canonical commitments and BIP340-authenticated replay-safe intake. GH-42/GH-44/GH-48/GH-52 supply bounded ballot transport, persistent identity, relay/AutoNAT operation, packaged sidecars, and explicit bootstrap routes. Merged/exact-main-verified GH-55/GH-58/GH-63/GH-74 add the independent canonical 2048-byte-bounded ThreatHint channel, development-safe Light Client builder, owner-only durable verifier ingress, a real manifest-pinned BN254/Arkworks Groth16 engine aligned with active KIP-16, and bounded digest/network/time-bound outbox adaptation. Merged/exact-main-verified GH-77 isolates per-job drain failures so failed jobs stay pending while later safe jobs progress; reports expose only fixed category/index and a validated digest or none. ThreatHint v1 contains no concrete IOC strings, so verified v1 input produces only an exact zero-confidence, no-rule, non-submittable result without invoking LLM or YARA generation; enum labels are never fabricated into evidence. Its caller-supplied hash is statement-bound but not protocol-derived from a file or observable. GH-82 specifies a separate artifact-hash and observable-commitment v2 design. Merged and exact-main-verified GH-86 adds isolated Rust/Python canonical bundle validators and one shared byte-exact corpus; these local utilities prove only structural and commitment consistency and are not wired into v1, P2P, proof, analysis, committee, IPFS, chain, or publication paths. Merged and exact-main-verified GH-114 adds isolated local canonical v2 statement parsing and digest parity without operational wiring. No approved production relation or production relation vectors, verifying key, or proving key ships yet, so unavailable verification remains fail-closed as busy. Real two-host operation, broad discovery, trusted membership/key assignment, Sybil protection, reviewed extractors/privacy gates, v2 relation/proof/pairing/transport plus real actionable analysis, on-chain attestation, real model evidence, and production operation remain pending. Phi-3-mini 3.8B is the Light Client target
- Observable production: merged and exact-main-verified GH-90 adds one local Rust `file_sha256` producer from exact caller-supplied bytes plus typed scope, with Python validation of shared vectors. It exposes no path, caller-supplied digest, generic observable, transport, analyzer, proof, wallet, or chain API and proves only deterministic function-boundary derivation, not external file provenance, maliciousness, privacy approval, or proof binding
- Merged review-required observable production: exact-main-verified GH-94 adds one local Rust `byte_pattern` producer from exact caller-supplied bytes, checked offset, boolean wildcard mask, and typed scope, with Python validation of shared vectors. It accepts no pattern string, requires 8..64 positions and at least eight fixed bytes, always emits local-only `review_required_v1`, and exposes no path, transport, analyzer, proof, wallet, or chain API. It proves no external file provenance, maliciousness, privacy approval, disclosure authorization, or proof binding
- Local ELF import extraction: merged and exact-main-verified GH-103 adds one Rust `api_import` producer from exact caller-supplied Linux ELF bytes and a checked index. It derives scope internally, caps input at 16 MiB and 4096 dynamic symbols, validates/sorts/deduplicates exact names, always emits local-only `review_required_v1`, and is independently checked by Python against shared exact-byte vectors. It exposes no path/import-string/generic builder, transport, analyzer, proof, wallet, or chain API and proves no external provenance, maliciousness, privacy approval, disclosure authorization, or proof binding
- Local Windows PE import extraction: merged and exact-main-verified GH-121 adds one Rust `api_import` producer that derives named functions from exact caller-supplied PE32 or PE32+ bytes plus a checked index. It fixes `windows`/`pe`, caps input at 16 MiB, 4096 import descriptors, and 4096 thunk entries, rejects ordinal/grammar-invalid imports, byte-sorts/deduplicates before selection, and always emits local-only `review_required_v1`. Rust covers both PE architectures and Python independently parses a synthetic shared PE32+ vector. Library names never become observables; no path/string/generic, transport, analyzer, proof, wallet, chain, or promotion API is added
- Local Observable Approval verification: merged and exact-main-verified GH-107 adds matching Rust/Python verification of one canonical, maximum-one-hour BIP340 statement bound to one exact `review_required_v1` bundle plus a separately trusted approver key, recipient-scope digest, network, report nonce, and separately trusted current time that must never be attacker-controlled. It contains no signer and performs no replay persistence, transport, promotion, disclosure, analysis, publication, proof, wallet, or chain action. The signed nonce and deterministic approval ID identify repeats but do not prevent replay
- Local Observable Approval consumption: merged and exact-main-verified GH-111 adds an owner-only fixed network/approver-key/recipient-scope policy and a separate owner-only SQLite ledger. Guardian Node invokes verification in the same trusted call path, then atomically consumes the approval ID and authority-bound nonce with restart, concurrency, lock, and clock-rollback protection. The local receipt grants no downstream authority and adds no pairing, promotion, transport, analyzer, outbox, proof, wallet, or chain action
- Local ThreatHint v2 statement: merged and exact-main-verified GH-114 adds isolated Rust/Python exact-canonical parsers and one shared byte-exact corpus for schema version 2 with separate artifact hash and observable commitment plus confidence, structural disclosure class, report nonce, positive observed time, and a network matching separately trusted local context. A new length-prefixed, domain-separated digest binds every field. This adds no relation, proof acceptance, signer, pairing, replay authority, transport, analyzer, wallet, or chain action and proves no derivation, truth, maliciousness, privacy safety, authorization, or anonymity
- Merged and exact-main-verified GH-117 ThreatHint v2 proof-binding, not production-deployed: strict Rust/Python canonical opaque-proof-envelope and 19-field `RelationManifest-v2` parsers plus one atomic separately trusted network/raw-manifest-SHA/domain/public-input compatibility binding. The two derived 16-byte digest halves are claimed inputs only; no Groth16 verification, source/key loading or approval, ceremony, transport, analyzer, promotion, wallet, chain, reputation, KAS/PROM, slash, commit-reveal, or rollout authority is added
- Merged and exact-main-verified GH-117 ThreatHint v2 Groth16 verifier, not production-deployed: silent Rust `verify-v2` owner-loads exact manifest/relation-source/verifying-key bytes, checks manifest anchors and canonical compressed BN254 encodings, and verifies only binding-derived field inputs. Runtime loads no proving key; all generated relation/key/proof fixtures are non-production, and no artifact/ceremony approval, approval consumption, privacy authority, chain action, or rollout evidence is provided
- Merged and exact-main-verified GH-117 ThreatHint v2 privacy/proof preflight, not production-deployed: an owner-only read-only policy pins network, BIP340 approver, recipient scope, and raw-manifest SHA-256; Guardian Node derives the statement only from the bound envelope and verifies review-required bundle/approval compatibility without Groth16 verification, approval consumption, SQLite mutation, privacy/disclosure authority, or operational side effects
- Merged and exact-main-verified GH-117 ThreatHint v2 verified-preflight composition, not production-deployed: a POSIX-only Guardian service owner-pins an absolute `verify-v2` executable by SHA-256, reuses the preflight policy network and manifest anchor, runs approval/privacy preflight first, then sends the same envelope bytes to a scrubbed, bounded, shell-free verifier process; its non-constructible receipt is data only and no SQLite access, approval consumption, production artifact approval, privacy authority, transport, chain, or rollout action occurs
- Merged and exact-main-verified GH-117 ThreatHint v2 atomic acceptance, not production-deployed: one raw-input-only Guardian service proves exact preflight/consumption network, approver-key, and recipient-scope identity before ledger creation, runs verified proof/privacy preflight first, then re-verifies approval ID and observable commitment before final durable SQLite consumption; failed verification never consumes or advances ledger time, and the data-only receipt grants no production artifact, privacy, transport, analysis, chain, or rollout authority
- Merged and exact-main-verified GH-117 ThreatHint v2 owner-policy promotion, not production-deployed: one raw-input-only Guardian boundary requires review-required disclosure, exact platform/format, allowed observable kinds, and a count cap before the same wires enter atomic acceptance; rejected policy checks never reach verification or consumption, and the restricted local result grants no semantic privacy, authority governance, production artifact, transport, analysis, publication, chain, or rollout authority
- Merged and exact-main-verified GH-117 outbox retention governance, not production-deployed: one pure owner-only Guardian loader binds an exact network/approver/scope policy and declares a local recoverable-analysis purpose, canonical bundle payload, allowed durable kinds, pending-record cap, and retention cap. It creates no database, outbox, worker, transport, or authority; any future recoverable enqueue must commit atomically with approval consumption and ledger high-water, while a digest-only journal is not recoverable work
- Merged and exact-main-verified GH-117 ThreatHint v2 enforceable governance, not production-deployed: one owner-only policy binds network, approver, recipient scope, authority epoch/window, fixed same-Guardian local-analysis semantics, denied external disclosure, and explicit deny-or-kind-specific-risk decisions. Promotion/governance/retention kind sets must match exactly; first valid governed acceptance atomically pins all three exact policy digests and authority state, while stale, equivocated, overlapping same-identity, replayed, or failed candidates change no durable state. This policy boundary alone adds no worker, transport, analysis, publication, chain action, or production artifact approval
- Merged and exact-main-verified GH-117 ThreatHint v2 durable analysis substrate, not production-deployed: governed schema v4 atomically stores canonical statement/digest, trusted nonce, canonical bundle, approval binding and retention with authority/high-water/consumption; claims revalidate all bindings and derive a lease-bound input identity. Atomic completion persists one canonical non-actionable result before deleting work and supports exact idempotent retry. Empty schema-v3 queues migrate; nonempty v3 queues fail closed unchanged. The bounded worker contains only a deterministic test analyzer with no confidence, should_submit, LLM, YARA/rule body, transport, publication, wallet, chain, reward, deployment, or external effect
- Federated learning target: Fed-DART with local records and bounded model updates; gradients can leak information, so clipping, secure aggregation, privacy accounting, authentication, and validation remain required
- Smart contracts: 6 Silverscript contracts on Kaspa L1
